chunks: From him, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Bint al-Walid ibn Sabih al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever blackens his name in the register of the children of Sabi' will be resurrected by Allah on the Day of Judgment as a pig."

key_terms.خِنْزِيرًا: A pig; symbol of disgrace or impurity
key_terms.سَوَّدَ: Blackened; to mark as inferior or remove from honor
key_terms.وُلْدِ سَابِعٍ: Children of Sabi'; a specific lineage or group

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of having one's name blackened in the register of the children of Sabi' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arab society, genealogical prestige (nasab) was paramount, and this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the severe spiritual consequence of being excluded or disgraced in the 'diwan of the children of Sabi'—a specific lineage or tribal register. The transformation into a pig on the Day of Judgment serves as a symbolic punishment, reflecting the loss of human dignity and status associated with this social erasure. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the preservation of lineage and the gravity of social humiliation in the eyes of God.
